name: autograd_function_requires_grad_check
description: Gotcha: torch.is_grad_enabled() returns False inside torch.autograd.Function.forward by design — do NOT use it to guard backward-save quant. Check input.requires_grad directly instead.
preconditions: Want to skip expensive bwd-save operations under torch.no_grad()
steps: WRONG: `if torch.is_grad_enabled(): do_expensive_bwd_save()` — always skips because autograd disables grad inside forward
RIGHT: `if a.requires_grad or b.requires_grad: do_expensive_bwd_save()` — correctly reflects caller intent
Under torch.no_grad(), autograd never calls backward() anyway, so setting up ctx state is moot — safe to always set.
Custom ctx attrs (ctx._my_flag = x) must be set unconditionally so backward() can read them without AttributeError.
expected_impact: Correctness — inference (no_grad) path skips backward-save quant (~1 ms/forward saved). Avoids silent AttributeError when backward runs but forward skipped the ctx setup.
failure_contexts: Initial MX-FP8 Function shipped with is_grad_enabled() check; crashed on first backward() call with 'FP8GroupedGemmMXFuncBackward has no attribute _use_mx_wgrad'. Fixed by switching to requires_grad check and setting ctx attrs unconditionally.
decision_rules: Never use torch.is_grad_enabled() inside autograd.Function.forward — always False there.
Set all ctx custom attrs unconditionally; guard the expensive operations, not the ctx setup.
